rationale: The merge is not model-type preserving. RBT-24 explicitly contains endothelial cells, pericytes, and astrocytes (a triple co-culture), MBT-24H explicitly contains primate endothelial cells with rat pericytes (a co-culture), while RTU states bovine brain capillary endothelial cells without either support-cell configuration. Product identifiers may be removable, but collapsing these explicit single/co-/triple-culture formats to `bbb kit` erases a protected assay/model distinction.

All 26 raw assignments explicitly describe a three-cell BBB/NVU co-culture. The decision retains the triple co-culture model type and in-vitro setting while removing only species, cell-clone, support, and named-protocol variation; no transport direction, disruption state, or distinct modality is collapsed.

Every covered raw value explicitly describes a BBB-relevant endothelial co-culture, including the BLEC, Cecchelli, species-specific, and stem-cell-derived variants. The common co-culture model type is preserved, and the removed species/clone/derivation/protocol details are represented outside this context label rather than being mechanism or direction states.

The six assignments state generic brain endothelial cell models and do not introduce an explicit monolayer, co-culture, flow system, transport direction, or barrier-disruption state. Normalizing bovine/porcine variants to `brain endothelial model` therefore preserves the explicit model type and removes only species or culture-protocol detail.

All four raw values explicitly say iPSC/hiPSC-derived brain endothelial or BMEC model. The final label preserves the stem-cell derivation and model type and only expands acronym variants; no unsupported biological or transport state is added.

All 28 raw assignments literally identify brain/cerebral endothelial cells or cell lines, with no explicit monolayer or co-culture imposed by the final label. Species, primary-versus-immortalized wording, vascular subsite, and clone names can be removed while retaining the supported cell-model category.

Each of the 16 values explicitly states a brain endothelial monolayer, including Biocoat and Snapwell-supported variants. The merge keeps the protected endothelial-monolayer modality and removes only species, clone, support brand, and membrane-material protocol details.

Both raw values explicitly describe iPSC-derived brain microvascular endothelial cells. The final label retains iPSC derivation and cell-model type without inferring a monolayer, direction, or mechanism that is absent.

All four raw assignments explicitly state an iPSC-derived brain endothelial monolayer or cells on Transwell inserts. Acronym, clone, and insert-brand variation can be merged while the iPSC derivation and protected monolayer modality remain explicit.

The two `other pampa` assignments state only organic artificial layers on a filter plate and never state PAMPA, whereas the companion assignments explicitly describe artificial membranes. Renaming the common class to `artificial membrane` removes an unsupported PAMPA inference and preserves the only assay context supported by every raw value.

The split is exhaustive, but it assigns `hCMEC/D3 monoculture`, `hCMEC/D3 monoculture under shear stress`, `human monoculture BBB model using hBMEC cells`, and `immortalized human BBB mono-culture model` to `brain endothelial monolayer`. Monoculture specifies the number of cell types, not monolayer geometry, so the child label adds an assay/model property absent from those raw values; the shear-stress record also carries an explicit flow-related state that the proposed child discards.

The two bare bEnd.3 cell/cell-line values are assigned to `brain endothelial cells`, while only the value explicitly saying `bEnd.3 monolayers` receives the monolayer child. Coverage is exhaustive and the split avoids inferring monolayer status from a cell-line name.

Both raw values explicitly state MDCK transporter monolayers. The MDR1-specific value is separated from the value that states only MDR-MDCK, preserving transporter specificity without inventing MDR1 for the underspecified record; both final labels retain monolayer modality.

All 12 raw values are assigned exactly once according to literal evidence: bare MDCK cells remain MDCK, explicit monolayers retain monolayer, P-gp/MDR1 transfection retains the transporter model, and the record explicitly saying type II plus human MDR1 is kept as MDCKII-MDR1.

The sole raw value is `MDCK_MDR1_BCRP`, which explicitly names both transporter constructs. `mdck-mdr1-bcrp` is therefore a clearer literal model identity, and retaining both transporters is necessary to preserve the transport-mechanism dimension.

The split deterministically separates three raw values that explicitly say monolayer from four values that state only MDCK/MDCK-MDR1 cells. It preserves the paired cell-model identity and adds monolayer only when the raw source states it.

The eight Caco-2 values are exhaustively separated into bare cells, explicit monolayers, and the explicitly bidirectional assay. This preserves assay format and transport direction and avoids retaining a provisional monolayer inference for bare `Caco-2` or `VB-Caco-2` names.

The split covers every raw value, but `LUVs mimicking BBB` is assigned to `liposome partitioning`. That raw value explicitly supports a large-unilamellar-vesicle/liposome model, not a partitioning measurement or mechanism. The split contract forbids adding information absent from the raw source, so this child assignment needs a literal label such as `bbb-mimicking liposomes` rather than `liposome partitioning`.

All 80 assignments are explicitly and exhaustively routed: records that state PAMPA remain PAMPA, explicitly BBB-qualified PAMPA remains PAMPA-BBB, Franz-cell artificial membrane remains distinct, and artificial membranes lacking PAMPA wording are not forced into PAMPA. Assay/model distinctions are preserved without direction or mechanism loss.

The 76 assignments are exhaustively divided using literal PAMPA evidence. Values explicitly saying PAMPA/PAMPA-BBB retain that major modality, while BBB lipid/filter membranes that never state PAMPA become `bbb artificial membrane`; the split therefore removes rather than introduces unsupported PAMPA inference.

The split is exhaustive but not inference-safe. `mono-culture hiPS-EC` is mapped to `ipsc-derived brain endothelial monolayer`: `hiPS-EC` and monoculture do not explicitly establish brain-endothelial identity or monolayer geometry, and the policy forbids deriving those properties from an abbreviation or outside model knowledge. `ECV304 cell layers` is likewise stronger evidence for a cell-layer label than for an explicit monolayer. These assignments need literal, less specific children.

The nine DIV-BBB records are exhaustively separated into baseline cultures, explicit hyperosmotic-mannitol barrier opening, and explicit MDR1/P-gp inhibitor treatment. The final labels preserve both barrier-disruption state and efflux-inhibition mechanism while removing only donor and inhibitor protocol detail.

All 38 MDCK-MDR1 values are assigned exactly once. Only the record explicitly stating AB direction receives the directional child, only inhibitor-treated records receive the efflux-inhibited child, and all other explicit MDR1/P-gp models remain baseline; this preserves direction and transport mechanism without inference.

The 16 monolayer values are exhaustively covered, and only the one explicitly pretreated with a P-glycoprotein inhibitor is separated as efflux-inhibited. Both children retain MDCK-MDR1 monolayer identity and no inhibitor state is inferred for baseline records.

The nine MDCKII-MDR1 assignments are exhaustive; only `MDCKII-hMDR1 with GF120918 (P-gp inhibitor)` receives the inhibited child. The split preserves the MDCKII subtype and explicit efflux-inhibition state while leaving all baseline transporter models unchanged.

Only the value explicitly describing plastic-grown cell monolayers is assigned to `bbb cell monolayer`; the other nine underspecified BBB/cell models remain generic. Coverage is exhaustive and the split preserves an explicit major monolayer modality without inferring it for generic models.

The raw value explicitly states both a primary rat brain endothelial cell monolayer and co-culture on glial cells. Renaming it to generic `bbb co-culture` preserves co-culture but drops the explicitly stated endothelial-monolayer modality, which the policy lists as a protected major BBB modality. A combined co-culture-monolayer label or retention is required.

All nine raw values explicitly say bovine. Normalizing the adjective to the common species label `cattle` is source-supported and does not infer a species from cell-line names, transporters, or assay abbreviations.

Both raw co-cultures explicitly state human endothelial cells and bovine pericytes. `cattle + human` normalizes bovine, retains both independently explicit species, and follows alphabetical atom order without inventing host/gene roles.

All 15 raw values explicitly contain bovine/cow and rat sources. Bovine and cow are lexical forms of cattle, so the merge preserves the complete two-species set and alphabetizes it without using cell-line or transporter inference.

All 88 covered raw values explicitly state pig or porcine tissue, lipid, or endothelial sources. Porcine is the adjectival form of pig; the merge retains the explicit species and leaves tissue/cell/assay context to the independent context namespace.

The sole raw value explicitly lists mouse, rat, and porcine brain capillary endothelial cells. The rename normalizes porcine to pig, retains all three species, and alphabetizes them without adding a role or species inference.

Both raw values are assigned exactly once. The generic `monkey and rat` value remains generic, while the other explicitly states monkey plus the scientific species name Macaca fascicularis and rat support cells, supporting the normalized `cynomolgus monkey + rat` child without inference from a cell line or transporter.
